query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Changing the percentage of elements in HfNbTaTiZr-HEA will significantly affect its mechanical properties due to the alteration of lattice distortion and atomic bonding.
generation.intervention: Variation of elemental composition by adjusting the percentage of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr
generation.mechanism: Solid solution strengthening and lattice strain hardening
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength and a 15% improvement in ductility compared to the baseline composition (equal atomic percentage of each element)
generation.baseline: HfNbTaTiZr-HEA with equal atomic percentage of each element (20% Hf, 20% Nb, 20% Ta, 20% Ti, 20% Zr)
generation.boundary: Composition range: 15-25 atomic percentage of each element
generation.uncertainty: The actual outcome may vary depending on the specific processing conditions, such as casting technique and post-processing treatments, which can influence the microstructure and mechanical properties of the alloy.

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of elemental composition and measurement of mechanical properties using tensile testing and microstructural analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured yield strength and ductility do not deviate by more than 5% from the baseline values for at least 3 different composition variations within the specified boundary, the hypothesis is falsified.
